name: VLTG // Corroded Signal Tour Tee
description:
The official tour shirt from VLTG's 2198 'Corroded Signal' run — a hundred and four shows across the Meridian corridor and three outer settlements. The shirt is a heavy 6.5oz cotton-analog in washed black, screen-printed with a fragmented transmission tower graphic on the front and a full tour date list on the back, several of which are crossed out with thick red ink (shows that were shut down by Vantablack security contractors or cancelled when venues were raided). The print has a deliberate degraded look — part of the aesthetic, part of the authenticity.

Two years on, the Corroded Signal tee has graduated from merchandise to artifact. VLTG's sound — a dense, confrontational mix of industrial percussion and melodic noise — soundtracked a lot of things that happened in 2198, some of them documented, some of them not. Wearing one says you were there, or you know someone who was, or you care enough about the era to have tracked one down. They show up at Shelf markets, Tier 2 secondhand stalls, and occasionally on Tier 3 bodies who paid considerably more than face value to acquire the credibility.
what_it_says: You have opinions about music and about what happened in 2198. You may or may not be willing to discuss either.
worn_by: people who were at those shows
people who weren't but wish they were
story_hooks: One of the crossed-out tour dates was a show that officially never happened — the venue doesn't exist in any city record — but people swear they attended it.
A Vantablack analyst has been quietly acquiring every Corroded Signal tee they can find and will not say why.
A character wearing this shirt is recognized on the Shelf by someone who says, 'You were at the Kessel Street show.' The character has never been to Kessel Street.
